headline: Members present supported a storage/salt shed building at 110 Institute Rd and a Legacy Fund land purchase, but lacked quorum for formal votes.
summary: The board discussed a proposed utility garage and salt shed at 110 Institute Rd (ZP-26-286) and gave informal support without a quorum. Staff presented the draft Plan New North End, noting conceptual development visions will be removed before a July 28 Planning Commission hearing. The board also discussed a Conservation Legacy Fund request from WVPD for a property acquisition, giving informal support and planning a special meeting to take a formal vote.
decisions: Deferred approval of the June 1, 2026 minutes because there was no quorum.
Board members present supported the storage building and salt shed project at 110 Institute Rd, though no formal vote was taken due to lack of quorum.
Board members present supported the Conservation Legacy Fund acquisition request from WVPD, with a special meeting planned later for a formal vote due to lack of quorum.

Conservation Board Meeting Minutes 
Monday, July 6, 2026 – 5:30 pm 
Remote & In-Person Meeting 
 
Attendance   
 Board Members: Rebecca Roman (RR), Zoe Richards (ZR), Alan Reichard (AR), Ryan Crehan (RC) 
 Absent: Dale Azaria (DA), Kelly Farrell (KF), Evan Horne (EH) 
 Public: Sharon Bushor, Marty Spaulding, Nick Warner 
 Staff: Scott Gustin (Permitting & Inspections), Dan Cahill  (Parks & Rec), Charles Dillard, Sarah 
Morgan (City Planning) 
 
RR, chair, called the meeting to order at 5:40 p.m.  
 
Minutes 
 
June 1, 2026 minutes 
 
Defer due to no quorum.   
 
Board Comment 
 
RR has seen ongoing communications around ash tree management.  Can we make a post on Front 
Porch Forum sharing information about EAB and give the city arborist an opportunity to weigh in?  RC, 
makes sense, especially given the Board’s role in tree management.   
 
Public Comment 
 
Sharon Bushor spoke to the Auer property item.  Any property acquisition needs to be in keeping with 
Burlington’s conservation priorities, even if the purchaser is not the city itself.  Should there be criteria to 
consider? How much money is in the Conservation Legacy Fund now?  I don’t know if what I’ve 
mentioned was discussed during executive sessions.  She supports acquisition of the property.   
RR said the allocation of Legacy Fund monies annually is 30% NBCS grant, 30% to stewardship, and 
40% for acquisition.  Staff is working on getting quarterly reports for the funds’ status.   
 
Open Space Subcommittee 
 
RR, we focused on the would-be pilot project for supporting native plantings in private properties within 
stewardship zones.  ZR, discussion included what’s under way already and whether there opportunity for 
coordination.    
 
Project Review 
 
1. ZP-26-286; 110 Institute Rd (I, Ward 4) Burlington School Dept / David Marshall 
Proposed construction of an auxiliary storage building and a salt shed at the north end of campus.
Conservation Board Minutes 
July 6, 2026 - pg. 2 
   
Marty Spaulding appeared on behalf of the application.   
 
Marty overviewed the project.  It includes two accessory buildings within the Arms Forest natural area 
buffer zone.  The two buildings include a utility garage and a salt shed.  The construction site is asphalt or 
grassy vegetation.   
 
RC, can they be accessed without further disturbance to the buffer?  Marty, yes.  RC said he appreciates 
that construction will stay within the disturbed area.  All Board members present supported the projects. 
 
Update & Discussion 
 
1. Plan NNE Follow Up 
Discussion of current draft of Plan New North End 
 
Sarah Morgan & Charles Dillard appeared on behalf of this item. 
 
Sarah Morgan noted the intent of tonight’s presentation.  A July 28 Planning Commission public hearing 
is scheduled.   
 
Sarah presented the timeline for Plan NNE.  The effort kicked off November of 2024.  Sarah Presented 
slides with some of the primary themes: sense of community, housing opportunity, multimodal 
transportation, place-making, and urban design.  She displayed a “focus area” map with 5 different nodes.   
 
Sarah touched on housing and community spaces on city-owned land.  It aligns with, and furthers, the 
Mayor’s housing strategy.  Significant additional study and public engagement is needed.  She noted that 
building on public land may make housing more affordable, fund the park system, and model what 
sustainable development looks like.   
 
Charles Dillard reiterated that a civic assets study is needed.  Engagement will continue with the planBTV 
2050 effort.  There will be additional community engagement at least through September 2026.  Park 
acreage and program replacement will need subsequent consideration.  He also mentioned the role of 
VT’s CHIP financing.  Reform the city’s process for procuring public-private partnerships.   
 
Sarah noted conservation-related revisions: Nature based climate solutions have been referenced, 
reiterates transportation framework’s alignment with the open space plan, states the opportunity for 
integrating OSP goals at recreation waypoints, identifies key ecological connections identified in the OSP 
as they relate to the mobility network.  It cites the need for additional community gardens, ecological 
corridor design guidance, and includes a map of ecological connectivity and how the two plans relate.   
 
RR, on pg. 14, reference to ecological framework for building on city-owned land.  What is that?  Charles, 
the recommendations are cumulative. 
 
RC, since you were here last, are there any significant changes?  Charles, we are not likely to include the 
development visions in the plan.  They have spawned significant confusion and misinformation around 
the city intent to build on parklands.  ZR noted the draft plans still include them.  Charles, they will be 
removed. The revised plan will be the focus of the upcoming neighborhood meeting on the 22 nd of this 
month.   
 
RC, what is the project timeframe?  Charles, the neighborhood plans have a 20-year time horizon.  It may 
change sooner, depending on changing environmental factors. He would like to change to a 5 -year 
timeline for neighborhood plans and to work on them, in different areas, continuously.  C harles, we would 
like to explore reintroducing a requirement for publicly accessible open spaces in the PUD standards. 
RR, in the urban design section, all of the community feedback sections were rewritten.  I’m curious to 
hear more about that.  Charles noted disagreement around parking at Starr Farm Park.  Some folks said 
more parking is needed while others said less is needed and that it should be bicycle- and pedestrian-
centric.
Conservation Board Minutes 
July 6, 2026 - pg. 3 
   
 
ZR supports pulling the conceptual development visions out of the plan.   
 
2. Conservation Legacy Fund  
Consideration of funding request by WVPD. 
 
Nick Warner appeared on behalf of this application.   
 
SG mentioned that this is an action item.  We don’t have a quorum.  Let’s aim to get a show of support 
from those present tonight and hold a “special” meeting just for this item before it goes to City Council.   
 
RR agreed on that plan.   
 
Dan Cahill noted his support for the acquisition. 
 
Nick Warner addressed Sharon Bushor’s comments from earlier in the meeting.  The property will have to 
go under a conservation easement.  Conservation will be in perpetuity.  The conservation easement will 
be co-held with the Lake Champlain Land Trust.  Access to the site remains in discussion.  It has ready 
bike path access.  The road is a dirt road that is basically deeded driveways.   
 
RR, do you have a copy of the conservation easement yet?  Nick, not yet.  Lake Champlain Land Trust 
are co-holders of the conservation easement at the former marina.  RR, be sure you bake in any 
anticipated needs into the easement.   
 
RC, some of our Legacy Fund monies have gone to the best projects like Rock Point.   
 
ZR, it would be great to put the Legacy Fund logo onsite to make folks awa re of the fund’s role.   
 
All Board members present supported the acquisition funding request.   
 
Adjournment 
7:03 PM.
